title: Kenyan Eid Chicken Biryani
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Eid Chicken Biryani — fragrant, golden biryani prepared for Eid ul-Fitr and Eid ul-Adha celebrations. Chicken marinated in yogurt and spices layered with saffron rice, fried onions, and caramelised cashews — the celebratory dish that breaks the Ramadan fast or honours the sacrifice.
longDesc: Eid biryani is one of the most anticipated meals of the Muslim Kenyan calendar — the celebratory meal that follows weeks of Ramadan fasting, or the feast that accompanies the Eid ul-Adha sacrifice. Chicken biryani for Eid is prepared with the finest spices, the best quality basmati, and the kind of loving attention that marks the most important day of the Muslim year.
ingredients: 1.5 kg chicken pieces — bone-in, skin on
2 large onions — thinly sliced and fried until golden
½ tsp saffron — soaked in warm milk
steps: Marinate chicken in all marinade ingredients for 4 hours minimum — overnight preferred.
Cook marinated chicken in ghee until 80% cooked. Remove.
Parboil rice with whole spices in generously salted water until 70% cooked. Drain.
In the dum pot: layer chicken, half the rice, fried onions, cashews, raisins, remaining rice, saffron milk, remaining ghee.
Seal pot with foil or dough.
Cook over low heat with a heat diffuser for 25—30 minutes.
chefTips: Parboiling rice to exactly 70% is the essential skill — practise before Eid.
The ghee is non-negotiable for Eid biryani — butter as a second choice only.
Saffron in warm milk: soak for 15 minutes before using for maximum colour and flavour.
commonMistakes: Insufficient ghee — Eid biryani should be rich.
cookingScience: See KEN204 for the full science of dum cooking. Chicken reaches safe internal temperature (74°C) faster than beef — the 80% pre-cooking prevents overcooking during dum while ensuring full safety.
sustainabilityTips: Free-range chicken for Eid biryani is both a quality and an ethical choice.
reheating: Reheat covered with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Saffron's crocin is a potent antioxidant.
culturalNote: Eid biryani represents the joy of completion — the breaking of the Ramadan fast with the most fragrant, celebratory rice dish in the Kenyan repertoire. It is also prepared for Eid ul-Adha, where the sacrifice of an animal is commemorated with a feast of generosity shared with family, neighbours, and the less fortunate.
